text:
Derek: getting multiple customer escalations — p99 SLO burn in hosted-infer-usw2 since ~03:12 UTC, lots of 504 / 502 timeouts reported. dashboards show a thin spike on gateway -> backend handshake.
Maria: saw that, digging into ingress traces now. dashboards: https://redwood.internal/dashboards/ingress/usw2?slo=tail
SRE Bot: ALERT: hosted-infer-usw2.p99_latency > 2.5s for 5m (firing) — incident id INC-4967
Support Jen: customer-reports: "calls intermittently 504, some succeeded on retry" — two different orgs in eu-west and us-west.
Aj: can you paste a sample request id / trace id? need to correlate logs + spans.
Derek: sample X-Request-ID: req-8f7a3c2b, trace: 00-4bf92f3577b34da6a3ce929d0e0e4736-00f067aa0ba902b7-01
Maria: query i did for gateway logs: 
```
jsonPayload.request_id=req-8f7a3c2b OR labels.request_id:req-8f7a3c2b
| jsonPayload.status, jsonPayload.upstream, jsonPayload.latency_ms
| sort -jsonPayload.latency_ms desc
```
Maria: logs show gateway forwarded to batcher V2 and then connection reset from pool after ~1s, upstream returned 502. snippet: `upstream_err=connection_reset; backend=hosted-infer-backend-2; attempt=1`
Aj: looks like backend returned early 502, need to check kv-cache & prefetch layer. adding `service:batcher-v2` spans.
Emma: tracing gaps — several traces for these requests only have gateway span and no downstream spans. tracer shows sampling=none for some. likely agent drop or sampling config change around 03:10.
SRE Bot: NOTE: deployment `batcher-v2` rolled out at 02:58 UTC to 30% canary.
Derek: oh — canary + new kernel selection change. rollouts page: https://redwood.internal/deploys/batcher-v2/rollout
Support Jen: customers also say they saw auth failures before timeouts (401 then retry -> 504). could be token expiry or authz proxy flake.
Aj: run quick log query for auth proxy errors: 
```
resource.type="k8s_container" labels.k8s_pod=~"auth-proxy.*"
| jsonPayload.status >= 400
| timestamp >= "2026-03-17T03:00:00Z" and timestamp <= "2026-03-17T03:20:00Z"
```
Aj: found spikes of 401s at 03:09-03:13 correlated w/ same request ids. token cache miss rate jumped 8x.
Maria: adding network metrics — tcp retransmits + handshake latencies for nodes in usw2. latency between gateway and backend pod increased ~120ms for a subset.
Derek: hypothesis: canary batcher + auth-proxy token cache miss -> extra latency -> backend times out -> gateway 502/504. tracing sampling dropped so harder to see downstream.
Emma: action items: 
- revert batcher-v2 canary to previous version (rollback to 1.4.2) OR pause rollout (canary: set traffic=0)
- increase sampling for gateway->batcher spans to 100% for 15m to collect repro traces
- bump auth-proxy token cache TTL and investigate cache eviction pattern
- enable deeper logging on prefetch/kvcache for 10m
Aj: running rollback now: `rbctl rollback batcher-v2 --to=1.4.2 --env=usw2 --sync`
SRE Bot: DEPLOY: rollback started by Aj at 03:27 UTC — job id job-9512
Derek: also enabling temporary fallback route to smaller model variant for low-latency customers: `routing:set --policy=fallback-small --duration=30m`
Support Jen: telling impacted customers: "we rolled back a canary and collecting traces, please retry in ~10m, we'll follow up"
Maria: increased trace sampling on gateway -> batcher spans (config patch pushed). collecting now.
Emma: added query to detect trace gaps: `count(spans where trace_id exists and span_count < 2)` alerting for > 5 per minute.
Aj: rollback completed at 03:32 UTC, monitoring for error rate.
SRE Bot: RESOLVED: INCIDENT INC-4967 — error rate reduced to baseline at 03:38 UTC (p99 back under threshold).
Derek: follow-ups: 
- formal postmortem to capture rollout safeguards for batcher kernel changes (need circuit breaker default)
- increase kvcache telemetry (eviction + hit-ratio) + add alert when eviction rate spikes > 5/s
- ensure tracing sampling override during rollouts for first 15m
Support Jen: will send customer update and collect any remaining repro logs.
Emma: assigning postmortem to Maria + Aj, due EOD tomorrow.
Maria: posting initial notes to /incidents/INC-4967 and attaching queries + sample logs.
Derek: thanks team :thumbsup:
